    - *Player*. The seal on the far cove stair. It has been walked on twice today. Good. That is what it is for.

    - Ulric. I carve the stone. My father kept goats on the clifftop. I learned these cliffs climbing after them.
    - I was Master of the Stairs once. Twenty-seven years. Then I gave it to Gorm. He argues with crews better than I do. I cut the hard steps now.
    - Old Struan took me on at fourteen. He made me sweep stone dust for a year before he let me hold a chisel. He said a stair belongs to the cliff. It only borrows the town.
    - He carved small things too, now and then. A shell. A knot. I took the habit from him. You are the first in a long while to ask where it came from.
    - A little animal on every step I cut. No bigger than a palm. A crab. A hare. A gull. A seal. Most people walk over them and never look down.
    - Fionn runs his shortcuts and skips half of them. I tell him he reads with the pages torn out. He laughs. Look at them as you pass, *Player*. That is all I ask.
    - The Anvil. The flight of Gorm's far cove stair that cracked in the frost. Hard rock, and broken. By daylight only, a little at a time. Gorm cuts the new seaward edges sharper. I have not asked him why. He will tell me. He always does, in the end.
    - Gorm told me, in the end. Now I cut the seaward edges sharper too. Stone can be taught to say no.
    - The Anvil is cut. Now I sit, and think about the last step of the Long Stair. The one at the bottom, by the quay. It has nothing on it. Not yet.
    - Go slowly. The steps will still be there.
